Redraws the cave walls on the bitmap ($6000-$7FFF). For every second pixel line from bitmap row offset $6282 downwards it reads the left wall's x from $0400 and the right wall's x from $0500, at index $41 + wall_row + line, subtracts the camera's x (the SBC operands at $82AF and $8323 are patched with $62 - 1 at $82A2) and clamps the result to 0-$50. It compares each with the x it drew there last time ($0A00 for the left wall, $0A80 for the right) and EORs only the pixels between the old and the new x, so the filled rock moves with the least drawing. One x step is half a bitmap byte (the masks $A0 and $0A from $0BA0); $0B00/$0B50 give each x's byte offset.

Goes through the level's objects, the list whose addresses start_level_tables patches into $8584/$858D and $880D-$8818 (x, y, type, flags; a type of $FF ends it), with each object's state in $A352. For each live one on screen it tests the player's four bullets against its hit box: a gun or fuel tank shot dies and scores, the reactor shot adds damage to $3E and silences the guns, a door switch shot opens its door ($6B). It drains a fuel tank the ship holds its tractor beam over (the counter at $07E0), lets the guns fire at random while they are not silenced, puffs smoke from the reactor, and queues every visible object's sprites. Object 0 is the pod on its stand. When the planet blows up ($6A reaches 0) every object explodes.

Starts a spark of kind 4 at the object in X, from the bullet table's position ($0620, $0660, $0680), through make_explosion.
Offset in x from a gun to its bullet's start, for each gun direction 0-3.
Offset in y from a gun to its bullet's start, for each gun direction 0-3.
Masks for how widely a gun scatters its shots, chosen by the low two bits of its flags: 1, 3, 7, 15 of the 32 directions.

Reads object $7A's x and y (from the lists start_level_tables patches into $880D, $8812 and $8817) into $7D-$7F and works out where it is against the camera ($03/$04, $62). $85 is set when it is in the camera's band of the level; when it is inside the visible play area it also leaves its sprite position in $AA/$AB (x) and $AC (y) and clears $AB's sign to mark it visible. For object 0, the pod, it also keeps its position in $64-$67 and its sprite position in $51-$53.
Operand: address of the current level's object x list, patched by start_level_tables.
High byte of the object x list's address, patched with $880D.
Operand: address of the current level's object y list (low bytes), patched by start_level_tables.
High byte of the object y list's address, patched with $8812.
Operand: address of the current level's object y list (high bytes), patched by start_level_tables.
High byte of the object y high list's address, patched with $8817.

Marks object $7A drawn this pass and queues its sprites through queue_sprite, by type: a gun is one sprite ($22 + its direction), a fuel tank two ($26 and $27) or one ($2E), the pod on its stand $28 and $29, the reactor $2A and $2B, a door switch $2C or $2D; colours from object_colours.

The sprite multiplexer's variables: $8933 next free offset in the queue at $0F00, $8934 sprites queued, $8936 set when a new frame's lists are ready, $8937 set while they are being built, $8938 where this frame's rotation of the hardware sprites starts, $8939 set for a text screen's raster list, $893A set when the play area is shown in hi-res, $893B the play area's background colour, $893C its third colour.
Number of sprites queued this frame (part of mux_vars).
Set by build_sprite_lists when the next frame's lists are ready; cleared by swap_sprite_lists.
Set while build_sprite_lists is working, so swap_sprite_lists leaves the lists alone.
Where this frame's rotation of the six hardware sprites starts, from the frame count.
Set for a page of text, so swap_sprite_lists puts in the raster entry that makes the play area hi-res.
Set while the play area is shown in hi-res (a page of text) rather than multicolour.
The play area's background colour (black, or a flash colour).
The play area's third colour, set per level from level_colours.
Restores Y, X and A from the stack and returns from the interrupt.

The game's one interrupt handler, reached through the KERNAL's IRQ entry and the vector at $0314. A raster interrupt is passed to raster_dispatch; a CIA 1 timer interrupt decrements $B46B; anything else is acknowledged at the video chip and CIA 2. All three leave through irq_exit.

Acknowledges the raster interrupt, then reads the next entry of the raster list at $0E01 + $AD: a handler number, and the line for the next interrupt from $0E03, which it writes to $D012. Advances $AD by 3 and jumps through raster_handler_lo/hi. A handler number of $FF ends the list.
Address raster_dispatch jumps through, written from raster_handler_lo/hi.
High byte of raster_jump.
Low bytes of the five raster handlers: $89C4, $8AA1, $8A3E, $8A4D, $8A8C.
High bytes of the five raster handlers.

Raster handler 0, at the top of the frame. Black background; when a new sprite list is ready ($8936) copies it into place (swap_sprite_lists); clears the multiplexer's counters; turns off sprites 0-5; counts frames in $1A and picks this frame's starting point in the six-sprite rotation ($8938); scans the keyboard; flashes the play area's background from flash_colours while $02 counts down. Then sets up the status bar (text mode, the screen at $5C00, or $5400 while $AF8E is 0), runs the sound effects (sound_tick) and the F1/F3 test, calls $3000, which holds only an RTS, and goes on into raster_handler_1.
Raster handler 2: waits for raster line $34 and makes the background black.
Raster handler 3, where the status bar ends: at lines $41-$43 switches to the bitmap at $6000 (multicolour, or hi-res while $893A is set), with background colour $893B and second colour 4.
Raster handler 4: turns multicolour on and sets $893A, so the next frame's play area is hi-res. Used in the raster list of the text screens.
End of a band of the sprite list: counts the entry and leaves the interrupt.

Raster handler 1, the sprite multiplexer. Takes the entries of the sprite list at $0C00 (five bytes each: pointer, colour, x, x bit 8, y) one by one into hardware sprites 0-5 in turn, writing the pointer into both screens ($5FF8 and $57F8), the colour, the position and the enable bit, until it reaches a $FF that ends the band. On the first band it skips entries according to $8938, so a crowded row of sprites flickers in turn rather than losing the same one.
Single-bit masks, $01 up to $80, one for each column of the keyboard matrix.
Background colours for a flash of the play area, indexed by the flash timer $02 (1-15).
Empties the sprite queue: $8933 and $8934 to 0 and an end mark at $0F00 and $07C0.

Adds a sprite to this frame's queue, unless 31 are queued already: copies its five bytes $A8-$AC (pointer, colour, x, x bit 8, y) to $0F00 + $8933 and inserts it into the list at $07C0, which keeps the queue in order of y.
Operand of the CPX at $8B96, which queue_sprite patches with the place its search found: moving sprite_order's entries down stops there.
End of build_sprite_lists: closes the last band and the raster list and marks them ready.

Turns the y-ordered queue into next frame's sprite list at $0D00 and raster list at $0E80: entries are copied in order of y and cut into bands, a band ending at the first sprite starting 12 or more lines below the band's first; each band gets a raster-list entry that runs raster_handler_1 above it, and the number of sprites a band holds past six is kept for the rotation. Sets $8936 when done, for raster_handler_0 to swap them in.

Copies the finished sprite list from $0D00 to $0C00 and the raster list from $0E80 into the live list at $0E05 (or, for a text screen, $0E08 after a raster_handler_4 entry at line $B8), unless a list is being built ($8937). Then falls into sprite_collisions.

Reads the video chip's collision latches. While $AF8F counts down after a respawn they are cleared and ignored. Otherwise the ship (sprite 7) touching another sprite, unless the rod was drawn in the last two passes ($4A), or the ship touching the background, sets $2A (ship lost); the pod (sprite 6) touching the background sets $2B, except while the ship's row $0B/$0C is below $178. Then writes sprites 6 and 7's registers from their copies at $9AB0-$9AB3 and $9792-$9798.
swap_sprite_lists for a text screen: copies the raster list in after a fixed entry for raster_handler_4 at line $B8.
The character for each of the 64 keys of the keyboard matrix, in matrix order (row × 8 + column), used by get_key for typing a name.
get_key's state: $8DAF and $8DB0 the last two keys seen (bit 7 set when none), $8DB1 the character to return, $8DB2 a checksum of the keyboard rows from the last call.
The key get_key saw most recently (bit 7 set when none).
The character get_key returns.
The keyboard checksum from get_key's last look.
Waits until the keyboard changes and a new key is held, then returns its character from key_ascii in A. X and Y are kept.
EORs the eight bytes of key_rows together, to tell when the keyboard has changed.
Clears get_key's memory of keys held, so the next call waits for a new press.
Colour byte put into the screen at $5C00 beside each character print_char_coloured draws.

The 5-line font the game writes on the bitmap: 37 characters (space, A to Z, 0 to 9), one table for each of the five lines of a character: $8E52, $8E77, $8E9C, $8EC1, $8EE6. FUEL, LIVES, SCORE and every message are drawn with it.
Second line of each character of status_font.
Third line of each character of status_font.
Fourth line of each character of status_font.
Fifth line of each character of status_font.
Moves the bitmap pointer $FB/$FC on one character cell (8 bytes).
Clears line 4 of the cell at $FB/$FC (the cursor) and moves the pointer back one cell.
print_char's way out: draws the cursor on line 4 when $8FD3 is set, restores Y, X and A and clears the carry.
Writes text_colour into the screen at $B5/$B6, steps that pointer on, and draws the character in A with print_char.

Draws the ASCII character in A into the bitmap cell at $FB/$FC with status_font and steps to the next cell. A space blanks the cell, $7F rubs out the one before, other control codes are ignored; letters of either case use the same capitals, and anything else prints as a space.
Clears the five lines of the cell at $FB/$FC and moves on a cell.
The character print_char was given last.
Set while a name is typed: print_char then draws a line under the next cell as a cursor.
Signed multiply: $89/$8A = $88 × A, each a signed byte. Sets the signs right, then shifts and adds eight times.

Moves the camera: adds the horizontal scroll speed $05 to the camera's x $62, and the vertical speed $06 to its row $03/$04, stepping the walls one row (walls_step_down or walls_step_up) for each row moved; runs move_doors. Then chooses the next speeds from where the ship is on screen: vertical in $4C (rows $20-$46 are left alone, beyond them the camera follows, at most one row a pass faster than the ship's own speed $16), horizontal in $4B (columns $14-$32). Finally, when the camera's x passes 0 or $D8, shifts every x (camera, ship, pod and bullets) by $AF or $51, so the level wraps round sideways, and flips the cached wall rows that $0A00/$0A80 hold so they are redrawn.

Counts the door timer $6B down, then, on the three levels with a door (the fourth, fifth and sixth, $A6A4 = 3, 4 and 5), redraws that level's door by rewriting its rows of the left wall in $0400, when the door is near the camera. After a switch is shot ($6B = $FF) the door's opening $6C grows a step a pass to its limit, stays open while $6B counts down, and closes with it. The three doors have different shapes: a straight edge 13 rows high, a 21-row edge with a step at the opening, and a 15-row point.
Takes one from the lives counter $9403 (in BCD) and prints it; returns X = $FF when there were none left.
Adds one to the lives counter $9403 (BCD) and prints it on the status bar at bitmap $59D1, as two digits with a leading zero left blank. (lose_life shares the printing from $9284.)
Adds A (BCD) to the score at $0180-$0182 (lowest byte first) and prints it at bitmap $5A21, unless the demo is running ($63). When the high digit of $0181 changes, gives an extra life (gain_life).
Sets the print position and prints three BCD bytes.
Prints the three BCD bytes at ($80),2 down to ($80),0 as six digits through print_digit, with leading zeros left blank.
Sets the bitmap address print_char draws at: X low, Y high, into $FB/$FC.
Works out the screen address for the bitmap cell at $FB/$FC (the cell's number plus $5C00) into $B5/$B6, where print_char_coloured puts colours.
Prints the digit in A, or a space for a leading zero (X still 0).
Adds 11 (BCD) to the fuel at $93FF-$9401, unless the demo is running. Called while the tractor beam drains a fuel tank.

Takes 1 from the fuel (BCD, $93FF-$9401), unless the demo is running. When it reaches zero, prints "0" for it, sets $9402 (out of fuel) and $57 so the ship no longer thrusts. Called on each pass with thrust or the shield.
Prints the fuel on the status bar at bitmap $5959, unless it is already shown this pass ($56) or the ship is out of fuel.

Prints the high score table on the bitmap: eight lines from $67C8 down, each "n.", the score (three BCD bytes and a trailing 0) and the name, from the table at $0100 (16 bytes an entry: score, then 13 characters of name), with a colour bar behind each.
The fuel, three BCD bytes from the lowest ($93FF-$9401). 1000 at the start of a game.
The fuel's middle BCD byte ($10 for 1000 at the start).
The fuel's highest BCD byte.
Set to $FF when the fuel runs out.
Lives in reserve, in BCD.
Prints "Game Over", the message at $0900, in colour 7.
Prints "Top Eight Thrusters", the message at $090C, in the gun colour.
Prints "Congratulations", the message at $0922, in the gun colour.
Prints "Please enter your name", the message at $0934, in the colour $AE68.
Prints "Press SPACE BAR to start", the message at $094D, in the colour $AE68.
Prints "Out of fuel", the message at $0968, in the gun colour.
Points $80/$81 at a message on page $09 (copied there from $B967 at start-up), and prints it.
Prints the message at $80/$81: two bytes of bitmap address, then characters up to one with bit 7 set, each with text_colour's high half as its colour.
Prints "Mission " (the message at $9515, at bitmap $6CD8) in colour $AE68, with a colour bar behind the line.
Prints "In" (the message at $9520) where the last text ended: with print_complete, "Mission Incomplete".
Prints "Complete" (the message at $9525) where the last text ended.
Prints "Bonus " (the message at $9530, at bitmap $70B8) in colour 7, with a colour bar behind the line.
Prints "Failed" (the message at $9539) where the last text ended.
Prints "No Bonus" (the message at $9542, at bitmap $70C0) in colour 7.
Prints "Planet Destroyed" (the message at $954D, at bitmap $6920) in the gun colour.
Prints "Reverse Gravity" (the message at $9560, at bitmap $6CE0) in colour 7.
Prints "Invisible Landscape" (the message at $9572, at bitmap $6CD0) in colour 7.

The messages between levels, each two bytes of bitmap address (low first; 0 for a piece printed where the last ended) and then ASCII text ended by $FF: "Mission ", "In", "Complete", "Bonus ", "Failed", "No Bonus", "Planet Destroyed", "Reverse Gravity", "Invisible Landscape".

Moves the ship's velocity on a pass. While the ship is not in play (dead, or before it appears) it is held still. Gravity: on 6 passes in 16 the gravity of the level ($A6/$A7) is added to the vertical speed $15/$16. Thrust (thrust_keys) burns fuel, makes the thrust sound and adds the direction's vector from the tables at $0880-$09BF to the speeds, a sixteenth of it, or a thirty-second while the pod is towed ($22). With the pod towed it also turns the pod and ship as a pair (the angle $1C/$1D and its rate $1E-$20) from the thrust's direction against the rod. Last, friction: each speed loses a 64th (horizontal) or a 256th (vertical) of itself.
Unless the ship is out of fuel ($57), either Shift key thrusts (on to $95E0); with neither held, goes on to the friction at $96EB.
Sixteen steps of the rod's angle, $10 to $F0, used to sum the direction table over the rod's angle in ship_physics and rod_vector.
F5 pauses the game when $27 is zero: sets $61 to 1 and waits, testing F7, until F7 is pressed, then calls $B45C and clears $61.
F1 stores $FF in $A2 (sound off); F3 stores 0 (sound on).
The ship's sprite registers as sprite_collisions copies them in: $9792 y, $9793 x, $9794 x bit 8 ($80), $9795 enable ($80), $9796 pointer, $9797 the shield's colour for the level, $9798 colour.
The ship's sprite x, low byte.
Bit 8 of the ship's sprite x, as $80 for sprite 7.
The ship's sprite enable bit, $80 when shown.
The ship's sprite pointer: its direction, or $20 for the shield.
The shield's colour for the level.
The ship's sprite colour: 7, or the shield's colour while it is up.

Each pass: works out the rod's vector (rod_vector); unless the ship is in play ($18) keeps it hidden. Space raises the shield and the tractor beam ($27, while not dead or out of fuel): on alternate frames it costs fuel, shows the shield sprite ($20) in the level's shield colour and makes its sound. Then turns the ship's position into sprite coordinates for sprite 7 (ship_sprite), with $4E-$50 a copy for the pod's distance test, and the pod's through pod_sprite.
Works out the rod from the ship to the pod: the vector at the angle $1C/$1D (sixteen steps of the direction tables summed, then scaled) into $23/$24 (x) and $25/$26 (y).

Picks up the pod. Unless it is already towed, while the shield/tractor ($27) is on and the ship is in play: once the ship has come within reach of the pod ($68 set by a distance under $75 from pod_distance), and then moves out to a distance of $84 or more, the pod is attached: $22 and $B512 are set, the two bodies' positions are averaged into the ship's (the pair's centre), their speeds halved, and the rod's angle and length are found by searching the 32 directions (three passes, each halving the step) for the one that points from ship to pod. Taking the pod also sets $A6A6, the level's restart point.
The pod's sprite registers as sprite_collisions copies them in: $9AAF colour, $9AB0 y, $9AB1 x, $9AB2 x bit 8 ($40), $9AB3 enable ($40).
The pod sprite y as sprite_collisions copies it to $D00D.
The pod's sprite x, low byte.
Bit 8 of the pod's sprite x, as $40 for sprite 6.
The pod's sprite enable bit, $40 when shown.
Puts the pod's sprite (pointer $21, sprite 6) at the end of the rod from the ship, while it is towed ($22); otherwise hides it. Its position is also kept in $51-$53 for the pod distance test.

Sound effect state: $9B44 volume, $9B45-$9B4A countdowns of the effects running (explosion, thrust, shot, ...), $9B4D-$9B51 the frequencies and slides they move, $9B52-$9B54 filter cut-off, resonance and routing, $9B55 and $9B56 the control registers of voices 1 and 2.
Countdown of the explosion sound (50 frames).
Countdown of the thrust sound.
Countdown of the shield sound.
Countdown of the shot sound.
Countdown of a gun's shot sound.
Countdown to the second beep of sound_beep_long: when it reaches 0, sound_tick sounds the beep again. Two bytes after it are not used.
The explosion's frequency slide, signed, reversed at its limits.
The explosion's frequency, voice 1's low byte, slid by $9B4D.
Voice 2's pulse width, low byte, swept by $9B50.
The sweep of voice 2's pulse width, signed, reversed at its limits.
Voice 2's frequency, high byte, lowered each frame by the shot sound.
Filter cut-off, low byte, written to $D515 every frame.
Filter cut-off, high byte, written to $D516.
Filter routing and resonance, written to $D517; its low bits say which voices go through the filter.
Voice 1's control register as last set (gate and waveform).
Voice 2's control register as last set (gate and waveform).
Return for sound_tick in the demo.

Runs the sound effects once a frame, from raster_handler_0, unless the demo is running: sets the volume (0 while F1 has turned the sound off), the filter, and voices 1 and 2; counts each running effect down, slides the explosion's and the shot's frequencies up and down between limits, and ends each effect by clearing its voice's gate bit. Every write goes to the SID through its mirror at $D500.
Starts a short sawtooth note on voice 3 at a fixed pitch: the beep of the reactor countdown, a fuel tank drained, the pod taken.
Starts the explosion sound on voice 1 (noise, falling) for 50 frames.
Starts the thrust sound on voice 1 (8 frames), unless an explosion is sounding.
Starts the shield sound on voice 2 (10 frames).
Starts the shot sound on voice 2 (25 frames, falling), unless the shield sound is on.
Starts a gun's shot sound on voice 2 (5 frames), unless the shield or a shot is sounding.
Two beeps of sound_beep_voice3, nine frames apart (sound_tick sounds the second): a fuel tank drained, the pod taken. Silent in the demo.
The beep of sound_beep_voice3, unless the demo is running: one beat of the reactor countdown.
An RTS, called when an extra life is given.
The keyboard matrix as read_keyboard left it: one byte per row, a set bit for each key held.
Scans the keyboard matrix: selects each of the eight rows of CIA 1 port A in turn and stores port B, inverted, in key_rows, so that a set bit is a key held down. Interrupts are off for the scan.
On a pass when $19 AND 3 is non-zero, A decrements the ship's direction in $0D and S increments it, wrapping to 0-31: 32 directions.

Adds the speeds to the position of the ship (or, with the pod, of the ship and pod's centre): $12-$14 to x in $07-$09, $15/$16 to y in $0A-$0C. While the pod is towed, or the ship is not in play, also turns the rod: adds its turning rate $1E-$20 to its angle $1B-$1D (32 directions in $1D).

Works out where the ship itself is: the centre $07-$0C plus the rod's vector ($23-$26), into $31-$33 (x) and $2E-$30 (y). Keeps the last pass's position in $58-$5B and the change since then, the ship's own velocity, in $37-$39 (x) and $34-$36 (y), which a new shot inherits.

Sounds an explosion and throws out debris from the position $88-$8B: eight pieces of kind $8D, or for a spark ($8D = 4) three pieces of kind 2 in a random direction. Each takes a free slot of the shot table, starts in its own direction ($8C, four of the 32 directions on from the last piece's) with a random speed of 2-5 sixteenths of the direction table and a random life, and is moved on twice.

Finds a slot of the 32-entry shot and debris table for a new piece: the highest free one ($0720 = 0) from 31 down to 1, else the highest whose life is under 10. With none, returns Y = 0. The random choice at $9FFB after it is never reached: the branch at $9FF7 returns either way.
Unreachable: would pick a random slot from 4 to 19.
Not called: prints A as two hexadecimal digits through print_char, keeping A, X, Y and the flags. Probably a leftover from development.
print_hex's copy of the byte it prints.
Prints the low four bits of A as a hexadecimal digit.

The first level's wall run lists, read by the wall generators through the pointers start_level_tables puts at $84C0-$84C7: run lengths of the left wall ($A03C), its slopes ($A045, one signed step per row), run lengths of the right wall ($A04E) and its slopes ($A055).
The second level's wall run lists: left lengths $A05C, left slopes $A069, right lengths $A076, right slopes $A080.
The third level's wall run lists: left lengths $A08A, left slopes $A09A, right lengths $A0AA, right slopes $A0BB.
The fourth level's wall run lists: left lengths $A0CC, left slopes $A0E2, right lengths $A0F8, right slopes $A107.
The fifth level's wall run lists: left lengths $A116, left slopes $A133, right lengths $A150, right slopes $A16A.
The sixth level's wall run lists: left lengths $A184, left slopes $A19B, right lengths $A1B2, right slopes $A1D0.

The first level's objects, as five lists (the addresses in $A95E-$A999): x ($A1EE), y low ($A1F2), y high ($A1F6), type ($A1FA: 5 the pod on its stand, 6 the reactor, 4 a fuel tank, 0-3 a gun facing one of four ways, 7 and 8 door switches; $FF ends the list) and flags ($A1FF: a gun's scatter in bits 0-1 and its aim in bits 2-4). Four objects: the pod, the reactor, a fuel tank and a gun.
The first level's object rows, low bytes.
The first level's object rows, high bytes.
The first level's object types: the pod, the reactor, a fuel tank, a gun; $FF ends the list.
The first level's object flags (a gun's scatter and aim).
The second level's objects, the same five lists: x $A203, y low $A208, y high $A20D, type $A212, flags $A218. Five objects.
The second level's object rows, low bytes.
The second level's object rows, high bytes.
The second level's object types, ended by $FF.
The second level's object flags.

The third level's object rows, low bytes.
The third level's object rows, high bytes.
The third level's object types, ended by $FF: six fuel tanks among them.
The third level's object flags.
The fourth level's objects: x $A25F, y low $A26B, y high $A277, type $A283, flags $A290. Twelve objects, two of them door switches (both type 8).
The fourth level's object rows, low bytes.
The fourth level's object rows, high bytes.
The fourth level's object types, ended by $FF: two door switches (type 8) among them.
The fourth level's object flags.
The fifth level's objects: x $A29C, y low $A2AF, y high $A2C2, type $A2D5, flags $A2E9. Nineteen objects, two of them door switches.
The fifth level's object rows, low bytes.
The fifth level's object rows, high bytes.
The fifth level's object types, ended by $FF: eight fuel tanks and two door switches among them.
The fifth level's object flags.
The sixth level's objects: x $A2FC, y low $A30D, y high $A31E, type $A32F, flags $A341. Seventeen objects, two of them door switches.
The sixth level's object rows, low bytes.
The sixth level's object rows, high bytes.
The sixth level's object types, ended by $FF: two door switches among them.
The sixth level's object flags.
State of each of the level's objects (up to 32): bit 1 alive, bit 0 shown this pass. start_level_tables sets every one alive.
28 bytes of zero after object_state that nothing reads.

Moves and draws the 32 entries of the shot and debris table ($0600-$07BF). First lets new_particle add one. Then for each entry: rubs out the two bitmap bytes it was drawn on last pass (EOR with the mask it kept); if it is still alive, takes one from its life, moves it, lets shot_hits_ship test it, and draws it again if it is inside the cave's open space at its row (between $0400 and $0500) and on screen. One that has gone into the rock is ended.

Tests the shot in X against the ship while the ship is in play. Player shots (kind 0) and debris (kind 2) never hurt it. A gun's shell (kind 3), and a kind 1 piece while the shield is down, that comes within a few pixels of the ship is ended, and unless the shield is up the ship is lost ($2A). A kind 1 piece near the ship is drawn in the other colour ($55).
Bitmap masks for a shot by its pixel position within a byte: $C0, $30, $0C, $03, two each.
The mask that sets each kind of shot's colour: $AA (or $FF on an invisible landscape, written by start_level_tables), $FF, $55, $FF.
Adds the velocity of entry X of the shot table to its position: x ($0600/$0620 += $06A0/$06C0) and y ($0640-$0680 += $06E0/$0700, sign extended).
While the camera is near the top of the level ($04 under 2), on even passes, starts a kind 1 or kind 2 piece, at rest, at a random x on screen and a random height below row $64, with a life of 30.

Starts a life on the current level. Blanks the play area, clears the game's zero page from $02 to $9F (keeping the demo flag, the ship's last row and the random seed), sets the life's flags (ship not yet in play, countdown off, guns silent for a moment), then finds the restart point: the last of the level's restart points ($A879 on) that is above the row where the ship was lost. It takes from it the ship's row ($0B/$0C) and x ($09) and the camera's x and row. If the pod had been taken the ship restarts towing it. With reversed gravity the ship starts nose down. Calls the music hook $A951 twice.
The level being played, 0-5.
$FF while gravity is reversed (each second round of six levels).
Set when the pod has been taken, so a restart puts the ship back towing it.

Sets up a level from the tables at $A8F7-$A98F, indexed by level: the gravity ($A7, negated with $A6 = $FF while gravity is reversed), the wall run lists, the colour of kind 0 shots, the addresses of the five object lists (patched into update_objects and object_on_screen), every object alive, and the fuel tanks full. Then falls into set_level_colours.

Blanks the play area and sets a level's colours from the tables at $A92D-$A94B: the play area's third colour and the text colour $AE68, the walls' colour in both colour screens and colour RAM, the guns', fuel tanks', reactor's and pod's sprite colours and the shield's. Then, at raster line $50, writes the status bar: character codes 0-$4F into the first two rows of both screens, and its colours.

Sets the play area up as a page of text: fills both colour screens with the colour of $D8A0 (the bitmap's foreground for the text), sets $8939 so the raster list has a hi-res play area, and waits for raster_handler_4 to have set $893A.
How many restart points each of the six levels has: 1, 1, 3, 3, 4, 5.

The levels' restart points: for each level six lists as long as its count, the ship's row high, row low, the camera's x, the camera's row high, row low and the ship's x. A ship lost restarts at the last point above where it was lost.
Low ($A8DF) and high ($A8E5) bytes of each level's restart point lists, and ($A8EB, $A8F1) of their row-low lists, which restart_ship searches.
High bytes of each level's restart point lists (with the low bytes at $A8DF).
Low bytes of the address of each level's list of restart rows (low), which restart_ship searches.
High bytes of the address of each level's list of restart rows (low).
Gravity of each level, added to the ship's vertical speed: 5, 7, 9, 11, 12, 13.
Low and high bytes of each level's four wall run lists, six of each: $A8FD/$A903 left lengths, $A909/$A90F left slopes, $A915/$A91B right lengths, $A921/$A927 right slopes.
High bytes of each level's left wall run lengths address.
Low bytes of each level's left wall slopes address.
High bytes of each level's left wall slopes address.
Low bytes of each level's right wall run lengths address.
High bytes of each level's right wall run lengths address.
Low bytes of each level's right wall slopes address.
High bytes of each level's right wall slopes address.

Six colour tables for the levels: $A92D the play area's third colour and text colour, $A933 the walls' screen colour (high half), $A939 the walls' colour in colour RAM and the pod's, $A93F the status bar's labels, $A945 the guns', $A94B the shield's and a fuel tank's.
Each level's high half for the walls' colour screen byte: 7 (yellow) on every level.
Each level's colour for the walls in colour RAM, which is also the pod's colour.
Each level's colour for the status bar's labels FUEL, LIVES and SCORE.
Each level's colour for the guns, the pod's stand and the reactor.
Each level's colour for the shield and one part of a fuel tank.
An RTS, called with a tune number in A and Y (7 and 1, or 0 and 0) when a life starts and stops: in this copy nothing plays there.
Twelve bytes after music_hook that nothing calls or reads.
Addresses (low, high) of the object lists of the six levels, which start_level_tables patches into the code: x lists ($A95E), y low ($A96A), y high ($A976), types ($A982) and flags ($A98E).
High bytes of the levels' object x list addresses, interleaved with the low bytes from $A95E.
Addresses of the levels' object row lists (low bytes), a word for each level.
High bytes of the levels' row list addresses, interleaved with the low bytes.
Addresses of the levels' object row-high lists, a word for each level.
High bytes of the levels' row-high list addresses.
Addresses of the levels' object type lists, a word for each level.
High bytes of the levels' type list addresses.
Addresses of the levels' object flag lists, a word for each level.
High bytes of the levels' flag list addresses.

Return fires, once per press. While the shield is up the ship cannot fire. A new shot needs its slot (the four slots 0-3 in turn, $2D) free of a live player shot. It starts at the ship's nose ($31-$33 and $2E-$30, offset), moves in the ship's direction at the speed of the direction table plus the ship's own velocity, lives 40 passes, and makes the shot sound; the collision latches are ignored for 4 passes.
Sets the velocity of entry X of the shot table to direction Y of the direction tables at $0880-$09BF.
Not called: puts entry X of the shot table at a fixed place with a fixed speed and a life of 40. Probably a leftover test.
Returns a pseudo-random byte in A from the 16-bit seed $3A/$3B, which it steps on (multiplying by 5 and adding 1, with the high byte mixed in). Keeps the flags.
Distance from the ship's sprite position ($4E, $50) to the pod's ($51, $53), through approx_distance.
An estimate of the distance from the differences in $88 and $89: three times the larger plus the smaller, at most $FF.

draw_rod's variables: $AB1E/$AB1F the routine for a step down or up, $AB20 the pixel mask, $AB21 and $AB22 the byte offset in the sprite, $AB23 bytes left in the sprite's row, $AB24 rows left, $AB25 which of the two buffers.
High byte of the routine draw_rod uses for a step up or down the line.
The rod's pixel mask in the sprite byte being drawn.
The offset of the byte being drawn in the rod's sprite.
The offset of the rod's start in its sprite, to come back to in the next sprite.
Bytes left across the rod's current sprite (3 a row).
Rows left in the rod's current sprite (21).
Counts rod drawings: its bit 0 picks the buffer at $5300 or $5380.

Draws the rod from the ship to the pod as a line into a pair of sprites, alternately in the buffer at $5300 (pointers $4C, $4D) or $5380 ($4E, $4F), and queues them in the colour $AE68. A Bresenham line from the ship's end ($88, $89) to the pod's ($8A, $8B), at most 47 by 41 pixels, stepping with routines patched in at $AC3D and $AC61.
Operand of a JSR draw_rod patches: the routine for a step down or up the line.
High byte of the step routine's address in the JSR at $AC3C.
Operand of the second JSR draw_rod patches, at $AC60: the routine for the line's other kind of step.
High byte of the step routine's address in the JSR at $AC60.
One step right along the line: moves the mask a pixel, to the next byte or the next sprite when it runs out.
One step down the line: three bytes on in the sprite, or the next sprite at its foot.
One step up the line, reached only through the routine draw_rod patches in: three bytes back in the sprite.
Moves the line into the next sprite of the pair, queues the one finished.
Works out the bitmap address ($72/$73) of the pixel at x $88, y $89 in the play area's bitmap at $6000, and its bit in the byte ($74).
JMP through an operand that materialise_cross patches: one of the four moves of its pen.
Low byte of cross_step_a's jump address.
High byte of cross_step_a's jump address.
JMP through an operand that materialise_cross patches.
Low byte of cross_step_b's jump address.
High byte of cross_step_b's jump address.
Draws one arm of the materialising cross: a square of $86 cells, each eight pixels of the pattern in $70, from the pen at $72-$74, then puts the pen back.
Masks of the pen's pixel within a byte for the cross.
EORs the pen's pixel, in the pattern $70, into the bitmap.
Draws one size ($86) of the materialising cross at the ship ($80/$81, $84; pattern $55) and, when the pod is there ($83 non-zero), at the pod (pattern $FF).
Draws the cross's four arms round the pen, patching cross_step_a and cross_step_b with the moves for each arm.
Moves the pen one pixel down.
Moves the pen one pixel up.
Moves the pen one pixel right.
Moves the pen one pixel left.
Draws the rod, or the tractor beam reaching for the pod ($45), through rod_ends and draw_rod; sets $4A so the collision with it is ignored for two passes.
The two ends of the rod in sprite coordinates: the ship's from $4E/$50 into $88/$89, the pod's from $51/$53 into $8A/$8B.
The level's text and rod colour, set by set_level_colours from level_colours.
While the ship is over a fuel tank with the tractor on ($3C), adds fuel and, on odd passes, queues the tractor beam's two sprites ($2F, $30, yellow) under the ship.
The materialising cross, grown in six steps and shrunk again, drawn and rubbed out with EOR, with a pass of the game between steps.
One step of the cross going away (or, for a ship arriving, coming).
One step of the cross, the other way round from $AECE: for a ship arriving it shrinks, for one leaving it grows.
The ship (and pod) appearing: the cross shrinks to nothing.
The ship (and pod) leaving the planet: takes it out of play and draws the cross growing.
Moves the pen four pixels down and four left.
Where the start-up code ends: turns the sound on ($A2 = 0) and jumps to start_game, so a game begins at once, with the player in control. The high score table and the demo come only after it is over.

$AF89 the guns' rate of fire, raised by one each mission from the third, at most $23; $AF8A 8 extra for the mission after a planet destroyed without the pod; $AF8B and $AF8C set once "Reverse Gravity" and "Invisible Landscape" have been shown; $AF8D the time before the demo starts; $AF8E 0 to show the play area's second colour screen at $5400 (with the walls black); $AF8F passes for which the collision latches are ignored.
Extra rate of fire for the mission after a planet destroyed without the pod: 8.
Set once "Reverse Gravity" has been shown in this game.
Set once "Invisible Landscape" has been shown in this game.
Passes (counted on odd passes) before the title gives way to the demo.
0 to show the play area through the second colour screen at $5400, where the walls are black.
Passes for which the collision latches are cleared and ignored.
Lets the player put a score into the high score table (high_score_entry), then goes to the title.

The title and demo. Silences the sound, sets the demo flag $63, level 1 with normal gravity, and shows the level's landscape with the high score table, "Top Eight Thrusters" and "Press SPACE BAR to start" over it. Waits; Space starts a game (start_game), and after about 280 passes with no key the demo plays: the same level, flown by the demo pilot (demo_controls).

A new game: the demo flag off, the guns' rate 1, score and fuel cleared, the name blank, three lives (4, less one shown), fuel 1000, mission 0, normal gravity and landscape. Prints the fuel and goes on to next_level.

Moves on to the next level, 1 to 6 and round again. After each round of six, gravity reverses; after the second, and every second round after, the landscape also turns invisible or back. The first time either happens, its message is shown for a few seconds. Counts the mission ($B673, BCD), raises the guns' rate from the third mission, sets the level up (start_level_tables) and starts a life.
Restarts the ship (restart_ship), sets a few of the demo pilot's timings at random, builds the screen (walls, objects, ship), makes the ship appear, and runs the main loop.

One pass of play: the demo's keys, the choice of colour screen, turning, moving, scrolling, the wait for the timer, the life's state, objects, ship and shield, the pod and rod, the sprite lists, the walls, firing, shots, pause, the ship's position, fuel and physics. When the ship rises above row $120 it has left the planet: the cross takes it away, and the mission ends with the pod ("Mission Complete"), without it ("Mission Incomplete", the same level again) or with the planet destroyed and no pod ("Planet Destroyed", "Mission Failed", "No Bonus"). Out of fuel, the game is over.

The end of a pass: RUN/STOP (or, in the demo, Space) goes to the title. When a life has ended ($43), takes a life: with none left, or out of fuel, the game is over; if the planet was being destroyed, the mission fails; otherwise the ship restarts.
Prints "Out of fuel" if so, then "Game Over", waits, and goes to game_over.

Each pass, the ship's life: counts down the time after a loss ($44), shrinking the rod and ending the life ($43) when it runs out; while it is in play, a hit on the ship ($2A) blows it up (and the pod with it, with the pod's own explosion), and a hit on the pod alone ($2B) blows up the pod, which is lost. Keeps $45, the tractor beam's reach, on while the pod is towed.
Works out the pod's position in the level: the centre less the rod's vector, into $5C-$5F, where its explosion starts.

Picks the colour screen for the play area: the one at $5C00 with the walls in colour, or, on an invisible landscape while the shield is down (and while the ship is in play), the one at $5400 where the walls are black. A destroyed planet ($6A = 0) also shows the second screen.
Sets $AF8E so the play area uses the colour screen at $5C00, walls visible.
Carry clear when the ship's row ($0B/$0C) is above $120: it has left the planet.
Waits Y frames (counting $1A); RUN/STOP goes to the title. Then resets the pass timer.

Hides every sprite and empties the sprite lists, calls the music hook with 0, clears the countdown's digit, the wall caches, the objects' shown bits and the shot table, and blanks the bitmap's play area from $6280 to $7FFF.
Paces the main loop: waits until the timer interrupt has counted $B46B below zero, then adds 3, so a pass takes three ticks of CIA 1's timer.
Sets the pass timer $B46B to 3.
One pass of ship_and_shield, pod_pickup and tractor_beam.
Counted down by every CIA 1 timer interrupt; wait_pass adds 3 to it. The six bytes after it are not used.
The same test as key_pressed, without the $63 check: always the real keyboard.

Tests one key. X is its number in the matrix, row times 8 plus column (A is $0A, S is $0D, Return $01, right Shift $34, left Shift $0F, Space $3C). Returns with Z set when the key is held. While $63 is non-zero, any key but RUN/STOP ($3F) is answered at $B49F instead of from the keyboard. What sets $63 is not known: it read 0 throughout attract mode and in play.
Key numbers of the five controls, in matrix order: A, S, Return, right Shift, Space.
The bit in demo_bits for each of control_keys' five keys.
The demo pilot's keys held now, one bit for each of control_keys; $B4C7 passes left on this step; $B4C8 the step.
Passes left on the demo pilot's current step.
The demo pilot's step.
In the demo, counts the current step down and takes the next one: the keys held from demo_steps and how long from demo_times.
$01 to $80, the enable bit of each hardware sprite, for the multiplexer.
The demo pilot's flight: for each step, the keys held as control_bits (A $01, S $02, Return $04, Shift $08, Space $10).
How many passes each of demo_steps lasts. $B508, $B50C and $B50D are rewritten at random at each life (start_life), so the demo flies a little differently each time.
One of demo_times that start_life rewrites at random each life: 8 to 11 passes.
One of demo_times that start_life rewrites at random each life: 4 to 7 passes.
One of demo_times that start_life rewrites at random each life: $7F passes, or $23 one time in four.
Set ($FF) once the pod has been picked up, or when the planet is destroyed.

Puts the score into the high score table at $0100 if it beats one of the eight (comparing three BCD bytes), moving the lower ones down. If it got in, shows the table, "Congratulations" and "Please enter your name", and reads a name of up to ten characters with get_key (Return ends it, DEL rubs out), with a cursor.
Not reached: a jump to print_char and an RTS after high_score_entry.
Prints A as two decimal digits (BCD), the first left out when it is zero.

The pod brought out: "Mission <n> Complete", then the bonus, counted up on screen: the level number plus 5 (plus 5 more if the planet was destroyed) lots of $40 added to the score, shown as "Bonus <n>00".
The bonus being counted up by mission_complete, BCD.
The mission number, BCD, from 1.
Cleared at the start of a game and by mission_complete; nothing reads it.
The game's first instruction, reached from the crack's relocator at $6C16. Copies 13 pages from $6C47 to $4000-$4CFF, resets the stack, clears zero page from $03 to $FF, then builds tables at $0B00.
The raster list's first entries, copied to $0E00 by game_start: the first line ($31), and entries for handlers 2 and 3.
Copies three pages from $B773 to $0400-$06FF, stores 4 in $AF89 and jumps to $0400, where the copied start-up code runs.

Prints the text at bbc_keys_text through the KERNAL's CHROUT until a $FF, waits for Space (get_key), and jumps to $0400, the start-up code. The text is the BBC Micro version's MODE 7 key page, with the crackers' credit added at its end. No instruction calls or jumps here, and no table holds its address.

Start-up code, which copy_startup_to_0400 copies to $0400 and runs there; nothing in it refers to $0400-$06FF, so it decodes the same here. Clears the sprite registers and turns all sprites on, selects video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through $DD00/$DD02, black border, bitmap and multicolour on, the bitmap at $6000 and the screen at $5C00; sets level 0's colours; copies the status bar's picture from status_bar_chars ($BB96) to the character set at $5800 and to $6000; clears the play area and the sprite lists; points the IRQ and BRK vectors at irq_handler (keeping the KERNAL's in $08C0); starts the raster interrupt, and CIA 1's timer A at $276A cycles (about 98 interrupts a second at PAL speed), turning the other interrupt sources off; silences the SID through $D500 and sets its volume to 15; and jumps to crack_start.

The high score table as the game starts with it, copied to $0100-$017F by copy_startup_to_0400: eight entries of 16 bytes, each a score (three BCD bytes, lowest first: 100, shown with a trailing 0 as 1000) and a name of 13 characters. In this copy every name is "SYNDICATE".

The direction tables game_start copies to $0880-$09BF: for each of the 32 directions, the vertical component (low bytes $B8E7, high $B907: $FD80 for nose up, so up is negative) and the horizontal one (low $B927, high $B947), signed, with the fraction in the low byte; the horizontal one is half the scale of the vertical, as a column of the level is twice as wide as a row is high.
High bytes of the vertical component of each direction (see direction_tables).
Low bytes of the horizontal component of each direction.
High bytes of the horizontal component of each direction.

The messages copy_startup_to_0400 copies to $0900, each two bytes of bitmap address and then ASCII text ended by $FF: "Game Over", "Top Eight Thrusters", "Congratulations", "Please enter your name", "Press SPACE BAR to start", "Out of fuel".

Text printed by show_bbc_keys_page, ended by $FF. It starts with 22,7, the BBC Micro's MODE 7, and uses teletext control codes ($84, $9D, $83, $8D). It reads "Jeremy's Thruster Game" (twice, for double height), "The keys are:" and the BBC version's keys (CAPS LOCK, CTRL, RETURN, SHIFT, SPACE, COPY and DELETE, Q and S, ESCAPE), then the crackers' line "Cracked By The Syndicate For TCI !" in shifted capitals and "Press the space bar to start".

The status bar's picture: 80 characters of 8 bytes ($BB96-$BE15) in the order they stand in its two rows of 40, then 128 bytes of zero. The start-up code copies these three pages to the character set at $5800, which the status bar shows in text mode with each cell a character of its own, and to $6000. The frame, the lines and the words FUEL, LIVES and SCORE are drawn in it; print_char writes the figures into the copy.
